title: Machine and Horizon
premise: Tamsin Lockridge smuggles memories past orbital customs and tends a beacon she never built, until the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream: a countdown, a reactor, and two fleets poised to annihilate each other over a war that ended decades ago. The beacon, it turns out, is broadcasting a fabricated armistice signal that has kept the fleets apart—and its reactor is dying. Tamsin must choose between exposing the lie that keeps her found family safe and forging a new truth before the countdown reaches zero. In the end, she sacrifices her smuggled archive of stolen memories to power an honest broadcast, and the fleets stand down as the children's dream finally goes quiet.
about_author: Juniper Amberdale is the pen name of a former radio technician who spent six years maintaining remote transmitter arrays in the northern archipelago. Their fiction blends hard-edged engineering detail with a deep tenderness for communities that live at the edge of other people's maps.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A routine smuggling run through orbital customs nearly unravels when a customs officer lingers on one memory chip too long. We meet her crew—the found family aboard the Kestrel's Wake—and learn she alone maintains the mysterious beacon. Emotional beat: wary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Dreaming Children
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Tamsin and Idris, a ten-year-old dockworker's daughter. Children across the colony report identical dreams: a red countdown beneath a black sun. The colony doctor quietly asks Tamsin if contraband memories could be leaking. Emotional beat: creeping dread beneath ordinary life.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Says
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She decodes the beacon's transmission and discovers it broadcasts a forged armistice—proof the war between the Concord and Meridian fleets 'ended' in a treaty that never happened. Her mentor's old logs reveal he built the lie deliberately. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as protection.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Sky
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Through the children's shared dream, Idris realizes they are receiving the beacon directly—unfiltered by the forgery. The dreams show both fleets still armed, still waiting, held apart only by the signal. Emotional beat: innocent clarity cutting through adult deception.

chapters.title: The Reactor's Honest Heart
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Inspection reveals the beacon's reactor is failing; the countdown in the dreams is literal. When it dies, silence falls, and both fleets will assume treachery. Tamsin's crew demands she come clean to the colony; she refuses, terrified of panic. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into secrecy.

chapters.title: Customs Officer Vey
chapters.summary: Vey's POV. The customs officer from chapter one arrives planetside, having traced anomalous signal traffic. She offers Tamsin a deal: full disclosure in exchange for immunity. Tamsin lies to her face, and Vey knows it. Emotional beat: two women circling the same truth, neither trusting the other.

chapters.title: A Lie Held by Hand
chapters.summary: Crew POV (rotating). The crew jury-rigs the reactor to buy weeks, not months, while Tamsin secretly plans to flee with her memory archive rather than stay. The crew discovers her escape prep; the found family fractures. Emotional beat: heartbreak of chosen family choosing differently.

chapters.title: The Children's Verdict
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The children, comparing dreams, reconstruct the true history of the war—including evidence the Concord fired first. They present it publicly, forcing the question: does justice outside the law mean repeating old crimes or breaking the cycle? Emotional beat: courage without cynicism.

chapters.title: Countdown Zero
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. With hours left, Tamsin chooses truth: she feeds her entire contraband archive—decades of stolen memories, including proof of the real armistice negotiations—into the beacon as honest testimony. Both fleets receive it as the reactor dies. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the only currency that buys trust.

chapters.title: Machine and Horizon
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating Tamsin and Idris. The fleets hold position, negotiating in earnest for the first time. The beacon runs dark but the colony builds a new transmitter together, children and smugglers side by side. Tamsin, memory-poor but unburdened, watches the horizon with her family intact. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
